sections.html:
Sandy tucks into Salt Lake County's Wasatch foothills, roughly 13 miles from downtown Salt Lake City. Population reached 96,904 in 2020, residents, a 10.8 percent rise over the 87,461 counted in 2010. Growth came mostly in one rush: 6,438 people in 1970, then 52,210 by 1980.

Land on the east edge climbs into the mountains. The west edge is flat valley ground beside the Jordan River. Views, slope and drainage vary between those zones, so buyers weigh a hillside property and a river-bottom property by different yardsticks.

One building boom produced much of Sandy's housing, which means original roofs, furnaces and water heaters may be aging out together. An inspector can date each of them for you, and that is worth knowing before you pay for any prep work.

sections.h2: Getting around: roads, TRAX and the Cairns
sections.html:
I-15 hugs the western side of the city, with ramps at 9000 South, 10600 South and 11400 South. U.S. Route 89 is State Street, and State Route 209 runs across town. Light rail on the TRAX Blue Line stops four times in Sandy. Buses from the Utah Transit Authority fill in the gaps, including a seasonal ski route to Alta and Snowbird.

  • Historic Sandy at 9000 South
  • Sandy Expo at 9375 South
  • Sandy Civic Center at 10000 South
  • Crescent View at 11400 South

A short walk to a station or freeway ramp is a selling point, so lead with it. Backing onto a busy arterial? Plan for buyers to bring up the noise.

The Cairns is Sandy's plan for rebuilding its center over 25 years across about 1,100 acres. Its master plan was adopted in January 2017 and splits the area into Central, South and East villages. City Hall and the Hale Centre Theatre anchor the South Village, while the East Village is built around the Sandy Civic Center station. We do not promise price effects from projects like this. What you can honestly say is that long-range planning and big projects are under way near the center.

Little Cottonwood Canyon is where Sandy's silver-mining past happened, and today it leads up to the Alta and Snowbird ski areas on State Route 210, a climb of about 8.3 miles at an average grade of 9.2 percent.

The Wasatch Fault also runs under this part of the valley. It stretches about 240 miles in 10 segments, five of them active, and a 5.7 quake near Magna on March 18, 2020 caused moderate damage. Hairline cracks in a foundation or chimney will show up on a buyer's inspection report. Cash buyers evaluate the property in its present state, so you can get an offer without paying for those repairs first.

Canyons School District has served most of Sandy since the 2009-10 school year, when it separated from Jordan School District. Attendance boundaries move from time to time, so call the district to confirm which school covers a given address before you repeat it to anyone. Salt Lake Community College's Miller Campus is also in Sandy, which some buyers like to hear about.

sections.h2: Permits, code violations and city services
sections.html:
The city website lists pages for building permits, code violations, garbage pickup, bulk waste, recycling and utility billing, and the city issues pet and business licenses too. If you finished a basement or deck and are not sure it was permitted, phone Community Development with the details.

  • Check the code violation page for anything open against your address.
  • Use the Bulk Waste program to haul off big items before you show the house.
  • Ask for a final utility bill and confirm no permits are still open before closing.

Unfinished work or an unresolved violation can stall a closing. Heirs and buyers-turned-sellers with half-done projects often find a cash purchase easier, because the buyer takes the history as part of the deal.

Salt Lake County sends Sandy's assessments and bills. Valuation is fixed as of January 1, and 45 percent of a primary residence's market value is exempt, covering buildings and land up to one acre.

StepWhenWhat happens
Valuation noticeLate JulyNew value arrives by mail
Appeal windowAugust 1 to September 15Board of Equalization hears appeals
Tax bill dueNovember 30Full payment expected
Reduced penaltyJanuary 31Penalty falls to 1 percent if all is paid
Tax saleLate MayParcels still unpaid are offered

If 45 days from the mailing lands after September 15, you get the later date. Bring a BE01 form and evidence of value. Submit online, mail it to 2001 South State Street, or deliver it to room N3-300 at the Government Center. Once a bill goes delinquent the county tacks on a 2.5 percent penalty.

If the November bill is still open at closing, the title company divides that year's tax between seller and buyer, and your share is deducted from what you receive. Mention it to the title officer up front and hand over your parcel number. An older delinquent year works differently: it has to be paid off before the deed can transfer, and the payoff is charged to you on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works, step by step
sections.html:
It begins with an address and a rough description of the house. Our offer comes back quickly. Lay it next to the net an agent expects from a listing once commissions, repairs and months of mortgage and utilities are subtracted. If cash wins, you choose the closing day, frequently within a few weeks, and a title company runs the paperwork. It clears the mortgage or tax balance and sends the remainder to you.

Bring photo ID, your loan payoff statement if one exists, the latest tax notice, and every key and garage remote. Heirs should also bring whatever proves they are entitled to sign for the estate. Nobody in Sandy needs to scrub, stage or paint for this kind of sale.

sections.h2: List, sell it yourself or take cash?
sections.html:
The right route comes down to the shape of the house and how soon you need to be done. Listing fits a home in good condition when you can live through showings and an inspection. Cash fits a home needing work, an inherited house, a rental with tenants inside, or a seller facing a hard deadline.

Asking us for an offer costs nothing and commits you to nothing. Weigh it against a listing's likely net, and walk away if the listing looks better. Ask for the offer in writing and read it through, including who pays closing costs and when you hand over keys, so the comparison is fair on both sides. A cash deal avoids open houses, buyer repair demands and financing fall-throughs.

faqs.q: Which county is Sandy, Utah in?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County. The county assesses Sandy homes, and tax bills and appeals go through its offices.

faqs.q: What school district is Sandy in?
faqs.a: Canyons School District, which has been Sandy's primary district since the 2009-10 school year. Confirm the school for a specific address with the district.

faqs.q: When are Sandy property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, and the penalty can be reduced to 1 percent if everything is paid by January 31.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Sandy home's valuation?
faqs.a: File with the Salt Lake County Board of Equalization between August 1 and September 15, or within 45 days of the notice if that is later. Include a BE01 form and evidence of value.

faqs.q: Will a cash buyer take a Sandy house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers can purchase a house in its current condition, so you do not have to fix the roof, furnace or foundation first.
